# Arachnids
Arachnids are a humanoid species with features resembling those of the common tarantula.
## Background
Years of human intervention and genetic engineering is what led to the birth of the first Arachnid, your ancestors are known to be one of the first successful experiments. Initially products of Interdyne’s researchers, your kind eventually bred outside of simple inhabited enclosures and began your own legacy, albeit heavily influenced by humanity's cultures.
Your kind are typically aloof and solitary, preferring dark areas and the maintenance tunnels of stations.
Tall, narrow-framed, and unsettlingly graceful, you move with a quiet precision that unsettles the unaugmented eye. Beneath synthetic dermal layers lie reinforced chitin lattices and redundant organ systems, gifts from both alien progenitors and human design. Fine filament glands along your forearms allow you to weave tensile strands strong enough to reinforce bulkheads or bind prey, a trait once exploited for industry and security.
Though engineered with compliance in mind, your neural architecture evolved unpredictably; you dream, you create, and you question. In the shadows of human megastructures and drifting colonies, the Arachnids endure: not as experiments, but as a people carving identity from the intentions of their makers.
## Unique Abilities
### Sericulture
- Arachnids can create Websilk at the cost of getting hungrier. They (and only they) can craft bundles of websilk into various items, from clothing and shields to entire walls.
## Diet
- They can eat raw meat without any ill effects. - They will get [color=#FFA500]poisoned[/color] by Theobromine (Chocolate, Tea, Coffee) and Allicin (Onion, Garlic).
## Benefits
- They have two additional Pocket slots in their inventory. - Their unarmed attacks deal [color=#ec3a3a]Piercing[/color] damage instead of Blunt.
## Drawbacks
- They [color=#FFA500]suffocate 50% faster.[/color] - their Blue Blood [color=#FFA500]can't be metabolised from Iron[/color], being based on Copper instead.
Despite their supposedly scary appearance, various species of spider share a fundamental kinship with Arachnids. Their bond draws them together and even allows them to converse in the same language.
